purpose: Exhaustive expected binder record for the R4 exports, derived by reading the FROZEN ORIGINAL sources. Consumed by binder_snapshot.py. The comparator FAILS CLOSED: any binder it cannot place -- an unknown extra instance, an absent required binder, a strict-implicit binder, a type mismatch -- is a FAIL, not a warning.
not_a_claim: This file is a specification for an inspection tool. The accepted evidence for the integration remains textual hypotheses + defeq + application compatibility (SignatureEquivalence R5, SignatureCheckFresh R5). Exact binder identity is not claimed by the integration; a PASS here is supplementary.

derived_from.rule: `omit` removes exactly StandardBorelSpace Y and Nonempty Y from the theorem telescopes; every other instance in the block is retained because the statement uses X (the measure space) and W (the factor space), and uses Y through p and g.

common.rule_unknown_instance: any instance binder whose normalised type is not in instance_allowed is an UNKNOWN EXTRA INSTANCE -> FAIL

FiniteEncodingApproximationAt.note: a def, so no omit: it keeps all nine block instances plus IsProbabilityMeasure μ

EncodingApproximationAt.note: Z is a value binder whose type is Type, so it is counted among the type binders; the comparator requires it explicitly rather than treating it as unknown

comparator_rules: absent declaration -> FAIL (fail closed), never inconclusive-pass
implicit binders: exactly the three type binders, in order, names compared
instance binders: multiset equality with instance_allowed; an unseen instance type is UNKNOWN EXTRA INSTANCE -> FAIL
forbidden instance present -> FAIL, named individually
strict-implicit binder present -> FAIL (counted separately, never folded into explicit)
total binder count must equal expected_total_binders where given

a type string that differs from expectation is reported as TYPE-MISMATCH with both strings; it is a FAIL for instance binders and a warning for explicit ones, because pretty-printing of hypotheses varies with pp options
